title: Spreadout of etaleness from the closed set defined by an ideal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if a ring map is etale at every prime of the closed set defined by an ideal, then it becomes etale after inverting a single element which is invertible modulo that ideal. The proof uses that the locus where the map is not etale is closed, writes it as the zero set of an ideal, observes that this closed set is disjoint from the given one, so that the two ideals generate the unit ideal, and takes the element appearing in the resulting expression for one: it lies in the failure ideal, hence inverts to a unit modulo the given ideal and makes the map etale after localisation.
